mcq.q: Which RAND report is considered the paper that started the study of computer security?
mcq.e: RAND Report R-609 (Willis H. Ware, 1970) is the paper that started the study of computer security and stressed management and policy. The closest confusion is the TCSEC Orange Book, a DoD document in the Rainbow Series, not a RAND report.
x: Not the answer here: RAND Report R-101 is not the paper the question identifies as starting the study of computer security.
The TCSEC Orange Book is a DoD criteria document in the Rainbow Series, not a RAND report.
NIST SP 800-12 is an introductory NIST computer security handbook, not a RAND report on the origins of the field.

mcq.q: Who developed the ARPANET from its inception?
mcq.e: Larry Roberts developed ARPANET; Ware wrote R-609, and Ritchie and Wilkes are known for UNIX and time-sharing password security.
x: Dennis Ritchie co-created UNIX and the C language at Bell Labs, so he did not develop ARPANET.
Willis Ware wrote the RAND R-609 report on computer security policy, not the development of ARPANET.
Maurice Wilkes led the EDSAC project at Cambridge, an early stored-program computer, not the ARPANET effort.

mcq.q: The DEFCON conference for those interested in information security was established in:
mcq.e: DEFCON was established in 1993, per the 1990s history entry. The closest year confusion is 1979, which the notes tie to the Morris and Thompson password-security paper, not to DEFCON.
x: Not the answer here: 1979 is not the founding year of DEF CON, which the question places in the 1990s.
Not the answer here: 1984 is not DEF CON's founding year; the conference began in the 1990s.
Not the answer here: 2001 comes long after DEF CON was established, so it does not match the founding year asked.

mcq.q: The DoD Trusted Computer Security Evaluation Criteria documents are known as the:
mcq.e: The DoD's TCSEC documents are collectively called the Rainbow Series.
x: The Orange Series is not the collective name; the Orange Book is only one TCSEC document within the Rainbow Series.
The Red Book is one interpretation document inside the Rainbow Series, not the name of the whole set of TCSEC documents.
Common Criteria is an international security evaluation standard, not the collective name of the DoD TCSEC documents.

mcq.q: The IPSec security protocols trace back to researchers working at the:
mcq.e: IETF researchers at the Naval Research Laboratory developed the SIPP security protocols that led to IPSec.
x: RAND Corporation is a think tank known for report R-609, not the lab where the IPsec security protocols came from.
NSA Fort Meade is the headquarters of the National Security Agency, which did not originate the IPsec protocols.
MIT Lincoln Laboratory is an MIT research center, not the lab the notes credit for the IPsec protocol lineage.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the seven critical characteristics of information in the slides?
mcq.e: The seven critical characteristics are availability, accuracy, authenticity, confidentiality, integrity, utility and possession, so non-repudiation is the one that is NOT on the list. Utility and possession are on the list and are the closest distractors.
x: Utility is one of the seven critical characteristics of information, so it is not the item that does not belong.
Possession is one of the seven critical characteristics, meaning ownership or control of information, so it is on the list.
Accuracy is one of the seven critical characteristics, meaning information is free from mistakes, so it is on the list.

mcq.q: Which characteristic of information refers to ownership or control of information regardless of format?
mcq.e: Possession is ownership or control of information regardless of its format.
x: Utility describes how useful or valuable information is for a purpose, not who owns or controls it.
Accuracy describes information being free from mistakes or errors, not ownership or control of it.
Availability describes information being accessible when needed, not ownership or control regardless of format.

mcq.q: The three-dimensional model of information security with characteristics, states and safeguards is the:
mcq.e: The McCumber Cube crosses information characteristics, information states and safeguards in three dimensions.
x: Not the answer here: the Rubik Model is not a recognized information security model, and the question describes the McCumber Cube.
The Bell-LaPadula model is a confidentiality-focused access control model, with no characteristics, states and safeguards cube.
The Zachman Framework is an enterprise architecture framework, not a three-dimensional security model with states and safeguards.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a component of an information system?
mcq.e: An information system is made of software, hardware, data, people, procedures and networks, so policies are not a component. Procedures is the closest distractor because it is on the list.
x: Software is one of the components of an information system, so it is on the list and is not the item that does not belong.
Hardware is the physical equipment of an information system, one of its listed components, so it is not the exception.
Procedures are one of the listed components of an information system, so they are included and are not the exception.

mcq.q: According to the slides, information security is:
mcq.e: Security is a process, not a goal, because perfect security is impossible and must be balanced against access.
x: Security is an ongoing process rather than a one-time project with a finish point.
Security is not purely technical, since the notes stress people, policy and procedures alongside technology.
Perfect security is impossible, so security cannot be achieved at 100 percent, as the notes state.

mcq.q: Which approach is a grassroots effort by systems administrators and seldom works?
mcq.e: Bottom-up is a grassroots effort by system administrators that seldom works because it lacks participant support and staying power.
x: Top-down is the opposite approach, started by upper management that issues policy, not a grassroots effort by administrators.
The waterfall model is a sequential systems development life cycle model, not a grassroots security approach by administrators.
Parallel refers to running work concurrently, not a grassroots effort by systems administrators that seldom works.

mcq.q: Which approach is initiated by upper management that issues policy and determines accountability?
mcq.e: Top-down starts with upper management, which issues policy, sets goals and assigns accountability.
x: Bottom-up is the grassroots approach by system administrators that seldom works, not one initiated by upper management.
A pilot approach tests a change with a small group first, a rollout method rather than a policy-driven approach from upper management.
A phased approach rolls out a change in stages over time, a deployment method rather than one that issues policy and assigns accountability.

mcq.q: Which SDLC phase is the longest and most expensive?
mcq.e: Maintenance and change is the longest and most expensive SDLC phase.
x: Investigation is the first SDLC phase that defines the problem, so it is neither the longest nor the most expensive phase.
Implementation is the phase where the system is built and installed, which is shorter than the ongoing maintenance and change phase.
Analysis studies the problem and requirements early in the life cycle, so it is not the longest or most expensive phase.

mcq.q: Which SDLC phase includes the make-or-buy decision?
mcq.e: Make-or-buy is decided in the physical design phase, where specific technologies are selected. Logical design, the phase before it, selects applications and data support, so it is the closest phase confusion.
x: Investigation defines the problem the system solves, which comes before any technology selection, so it is not the make-or-buy phase.
Analysis studies requirements and feasibility before design, so it does not include the technology selection of make-or-buy.
Maintenance and change is the final ongoing phase, after the system is built, so the make-or-buy decision does not happen there.

mcq.q: Which SDLC phase asks "What problem is the system being developed to solve?"
mcq.e: Investigation asks what problem the system is being developed to solve.
x: Logical design specifies what the system will do and which applications and data support it, not the problem being solved.
Implementation is the phase where the designed system is built and installed, which comes after the problem is defined.
Analysis studies the requirements and feasibility after investigation has defined the problem, so it does not ask this question first.

mcq.q: Establishing procedures to create software that is more capable of being deployed securely is called:
mcq.e: Software assurance is secure-development planning within the SDLC so software can be deployed securely.
x: Software piracy is the illegal copying or use of software, not planning for secure development and deployment.
Software reuse means using existing components again, which does not describe procedures for secure deployment.
Software testing checks software for defects, a part of assurance, but not the broader secure-development procedures the question describes.

mcq.q: Which NIST publication covers security considerations in the system development life cycle?
mcq.e: NIST SP 800-64 covers security considerations in the system development life cycle. SP 800-14 (33 principles) and SP 800-30 (risk) are the closest NIST publication confusions.
x: NIST SP 800-14 lists generally accepted principles for securing IT systems, not the SDLC security publication.
NIST SP 800-30 is the guide for conducting risk assessments, not the publication on SDLC security considerations.
NIST SP 800-12 is an introductory computer security handbook, not the publication covering SDLC security.

mcq.q: Sanitization of media is a key security activity in which NIST SDLC phase?
mcq.e: Disposal is the last phase of the NIST SDLC and includes archiving information and sanitizing media.
x: Initiation is the first NIST SDLC phase for planning, which comes long before media is sanitized at the end of the life cycle.
Implementation and Assessment is the phase where the system is tested and authorized, before the system is retired and its media sanitized.
Operations and maintenance is the phase where the system runs and is maintained, before it is retired and its media is sanitized.

mcq.q: Which executive is usually responsible for assessment, management and implementation of information security and reports to the CIO?
mcq.e: The CISO is primarily responsible for assessing, managing and implementing information security and usually reports to the CIO.
x: The CEO is the chief executive, a top role that does not usually handle day-to-day security management reporting to the CIO.
The CFO is the chief financial officer, responsible for finance rather than information security management.
The COO is the chief operating officer, responsible for operations rather than the security role that reports to the CIO.

mcq.q: Senior management responsible for the security and use of a particular set of information are the:
mcq.e: Data owners are the senior managers responsible for the security and use of a set of information.
x: Data custodians handle the systems that store and process data, not the senior responsibility for its security and use.
Data users are the people who work with information in their jobs, without the senior responsibility for its security.
Not the answer here: data analysts examine data for insight, not senior management responsibility for the security and use of information.

mcq.q: Those responsible for the information and systems that process, transmit and store it are the:
mcq.e: Data custodians are responsible for the information and the systems that process, transmit and store it.
x: Data owners are the senior managers accountable for the security and use of information, not the systems that handle it.
Data users are the people who work with the information, not those responsible for the systems that process it.
Not the answer here: data brokers trade or sell data commercially, which is not the custodial role the question describes.

mcq.q: Security that "begins and ends with the people who interact with the system" is viewed as:
mcq.e: Security begins and ends with the people who interact with the system, which makes it a social science.
x: Art refers to creative skill, but the notes classify security centered on people as a social science rather than an art.
A pure science rests on exact laws and measurement, while security that begins and ends with people is a social science.
A legal requirement is a compliance obligation, not the discipline the question describes, which is classified as social science.

mcq.q: How many categories of threats to information security are listed in Table 2-5 of the slides?
mcq.e: Table 2-5 lists 12 threat categories (IP, quality of service, espionage, forces of nature, human error, extortion, sabotage, software attacks, hardware failures, software failures, obsolescence, theft), so 8, 10 and 14 are not the count.
x: Does not match the twelve threat categories counted in Table 2-5 of the slides.
Does not match the twelve threat categories counted in Table 2-5 of the slides.
Does not match the twelve threat categories counted in Table 2-5 of the slides.

mcq.q: Which threat category includes piracy and copyright infringement?
mcq.e: Piracy and copyright infringement fall under compromises to intellectual property.
x: Espionage or trespass covers unauthorized access to or spying on information, not copyright and piracy violations.
Theft is the taking of assets, which is not the category the notes use for piracy and copyright infringement.
Sabotage or vandalism is deliberate destruction or defacement, not copyright infringement.

mcq.q: Which two watchdog organizations investigate software abuse?
mcq.e: SIIA (Software & Information Industry Association) and BSA (Business Software Alliance) are the software-industry watchdogs that investigate software abuse. ISACA and ISSA are professional security organizations, the closest confusion, but they are not the software-piracy watchdogs.
x: ISACA and ISSA are professional security and audit associations, not the software-industry watchdogs for software abuse.
ACM and IEEE are computing professional societies, not organizations that investigate software piracy.
SANS and CERT are security training and incident-response organizations, not the software-industry watchdogs.

mcq.q: Power excess, shortage and loss are examples of:
mcq.e: Power excesses, shortages and losses are power irregularities, which count as deviations in quality of service.
x: Forces of nature are natural events such as floods or fires, not the power irregularities the question describes.
Information extortion is an attacker demanding payment for stolen information, not power excess, shortage or loss.
Technological obsolescence is a threat from antiquated technology, a separate category from power irregularities.

mcq.q: Competitive intelligence is legal, whereas the illegal counterpart is:
mcq.e: Competitive intelligence is legal; industrial espionage is its illegal counterpart.
x: Shoulder surfing is observing someone's screen or input, a social tactic rather than the illegal counterpart of competitive intelligence.
Phreaking is hacking telephone systems, not the corporate information gathering the question describes.
Pharming redirects users to fake sites through DNS or host file tampering, not the illegal counterpart of competitive intelligence.

mcq.q: An individual who hacks the public telephone system to make free calls is a:
mcq.e: A phreaker hacks the public telephone system. The closest confusion is the cracker, who removes software copy protection.
x: A cracker breaks software or system security, which is not the same as hacking the public telephone system.
A hacktivist attacks targets for political or social causes, not to make free phone calls.
A script kiddie uses existing tools without deep skill, which does not define someone who hacks telephone systems.

mcq.q: A person who removes software protection designed to prevent unauthorized duplication is a:
mcq.e: A cracker removes software protection designed to prevent unauthorized duplication. The closest confusion is the phreaker, who targets the phone system.
x: A phreaker hacks the public telephone system, not software copy protection.
A white hat is an ethical security tester, not someone who removes software copy protection.
An insider is a person within an organization who misuses access, which is not defined by removing software protection.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a password attack in the slides?
mcq.e: Pharming redirects users to a fake site through the browser address bar, so it is not a password attack, while brute force, dictionary and rainbow tables are. Pharming is the one NOT listed among the password attacks in the notes.
x: Brute force tries every possible password, so it is a password attack and not the item that does not belong.
Dictionary attacks try words from a list as passwords, so they are a password attack and are included.
Rainbow tables are precomputed hash tables used to crack passwords, so they are a password attack and not the exception.

mcq.q: The quote "People are the weakest link" is attributed to:
mcq.e: The notes attribute the quote that people are the weakest link to Kevin Mitnick. Bruce Schneier is the closest name confusion, a security figure who is not the attribution in the notes.
x: Bruce Schneier is a security cryptographer and author, not the source of this quote in the notes.
Kevin Poulsen is a hacker known for telephone system exploits, not the attribution of this quote.
Vint Cerf is a co-designer of the TCP/IP protocols, not the person quoted here.

mcq.q: The Nigerian 4-1-9 letter is an example of:
mcq.e: The Nigerian 4-1-9 letter is advance-fee fraud, a form of social engineering.
x: Phishing uses fraudulent messages or sites to steal credentials, not to collect upfront fees.
Pharming redirects users to fake sites through the address bar or name lookup, not an upfront fee scheme.
Spoofing impersonates a trusted identity or address, not a scheme asking victims to pay fees in advance.

mcq.q: An attacker steals information and demands compensation for its return or nondisclosure. This is:
mcq.e: Information extortion is stealing information and demanding payment for its return or nondisclosure.
x: Sabotage is deliberate disruption or destruction of systems, not demanding payment for stolen information.
Espionage is secret gathering of information, without the demand for compensation the question describes.
Vandalism is deliberate damage to property, not extortion for stolen information.

mcq.q: Website defacing is an example of:
mcq.e: Defacing a website is sabotage or vandalism.
x: Theft is the unlawful taking of assets, not the defacing or damaging of a website.
Human error is an accidental mistake, not intentional defacement of a website.
Forces of nature are natural events, not an attacker's deliberate act of defacing a site.

mcq.q: Code segments that attach to an existing program and take control of access to the target computer are:
mcq.e: A virus attaches to an existing program and takes control of access to the target computer.
x: Worms are self-replicating programs that spread on their own rather than attaching to an existing program.
Trojan horses are malware disguised as legitimate software, not code that attaches to existing programs.
Back doors are hidden access paths into a system, not code segments that attach to a program.

mcq.q: Malware that replicates itself until it fills available memory and disk space is a:
mcq.e: A worm replicates itself until it fills available memory and disk space.
x: A virus attaches to a host program and needs it to spread, so it does not replicate itself independently.
A Trojan horse is malware disguised as legitimate software and does not replicate itself.
A hoax is a false warning message rather than malware code that replicates itself.

mcq.q: Malware disguised as helpful or necessary software is a:
mcq.e: A Trojan horse is malware disguised as helpful or necessary software.
x: A worm spreads independently by replicating itself, rather than being disguised as helpful software.
A virus attaches to an existing program, rather than being disguised as helpful or necessary software.
A back door is a hidden access route into a system, not malware disguised as helpful software.

mcq.q: Malware that actually evolves to elude detection is called:
mcq.e: A polymorphic threat changes over time to evade detection.
x: A virus hoax is a false warning about a virus, not malware that changes itself to evade detection.
A back door is a hidden access route, not code that evolves to elude detection.
A packet sniffer is a tool that captures network traffic, not malware that evolves to evade detection.

mcq.q: Gaining access using a known or newly discovered access mechanism describes a:
mcq.e: A back door is access through a known or newly discovered mechanism that bypasses normal controls.
x: DDoS is a coordinated flood of traffic that denies service, not access gained through a known mechanism.
Spoofing is impersonating a trusted address or identity, not gaining access through a known mechanism.
A mail bomb floods an inbox with messages, not access gained through a known or discovered mechanism.

mcq.q: A coordinated stream of requests launched from many locations simultaneously is a:
mcq.e: A DDoS is a coordinated denial-of-service attack launched from many locations at once.
x: A DoS attack comes from a single source, while the question describes requests launched from many locations at once.
A mail bomb floods a target with e-mail, not a coordinated stream from many locations.
Spoofing impersonates a trusted address, not a coordinated stream of requests from many locations.

mcq.q: Routing large quantities of e-mail to a target to overwhelm the receiver is a:
mcq.e: A mail bomb routes a huge volume of e-mail to a target to overwhelm it, which is a form of DoS.
x: Phishing uses deceptive messages to steal credentials, not to overwhelm a receiver with volume.
Spam is unsolicited bulk e-mail, not a deliberate targeted overload of one receiver.
Pharming redirects users to fake sites, not a flood of e-mail to overwhelm a target.

mcq.q: A technique in which the intruder assumes a trusted IP address is:
mcq.e: Spoofing is when an intruder assumes a trusted IP address.
x: Pharming redirects users to fake sites through the browser or name lookup, not assuming a trusted IP address.
Sniffing captures traffic on a network, not assuming a trusted IP address.
Phishing is a social-engineering attack that tricks users into giving up credentials, not assuming a trusted IP address.

mcq.q: An attack on a browser's address bar to redirect users to an illegitimate site is:
mcq.e: Pharming attacks the browser address bar or name lookup to send users to a fake site. Phishing is the closest confusion; it is a social-engineering attack, listed separately in the notes.
x: Spoofing impersonates a trusted identity or address, rather than redirecting users through the browser address bar.
Phishing is a social-engineering message that tricks users, not an attack on the browser address bar.
Sniffing captures network traffic, not redirection of users to an illegitimate site.

mcq.q: An attacker monitors packets, modifies them and inserts them back into the network. This is:
mcq.e: In a man-in-the-middle attack the attacker monitors, modifies and re-inserts packets.
x: A replay attack resends captured valid messages later, rather than monitoring, modifying and reinserting packets in real time.
A Smurf attack is an amplified ICMP flood that denies service, not monitoring and modifying packets.
A teardrop attack exploits overlapping IP fragments to crash a system, not monitoring and modifying packets.

mcq.q: A tool that monitors data traveling over a network and can be used legitimately or for theft is a:
mcq.e: A packet sniffer monitors data on a network and can be legitimate or used for theft.
x: A port scanner probes a host for open ports rather than monitoring data traveling over the network.
A vulnerability scanner looks for weaknesses in systems, not for monitoring data traveling over the network.
A honeypot is a decoy system meant to attract attackers, not a tool that monitors network data.

mcq.q: Which malware in the slides' table is a macro virus?
mcq.e: Melissa (1999) is the macro virus in the malware table. Code Red, Sobig F and Conficker are worms, the closest confusion, so they are not the answer.
x: Code Red is a worm that exploits IIS servers, not a macro virus.
Sobig F is a mass-mailing worm, not the macro virus in the slides' table.
Conficker is a worm that exploits Windows service flaws, not a macro virus.

mcq.q: MTBF in hardware reliability stands for:
mcq.e: MTBF is mean time between failure, a hardware reliability measure.
x: Maximum time before failure is not the standard hardware reliability measure MTBF stands for.
Minimum time to backup failure is not a standard hardware reliability term, so it does not match MTBF.
Mean time to boot failure is not the standard hardware reliability term, so it does not match MTBF.

mcq.q: Which organization publishes a list of top web application security risks?
mcq.e: OWASP publishes lists of the top web application security risks.
x: BSA is a software-industry watchdog that investigates software piracy, not the publisher of web application security risk lists.
SIIA is the Software and Information Industry Association, a software-industry group, not the publisher of web security risk lists.
CERT is a security incident-response coordination center, not the publisher of the OWASP top web application risks.

mcq.q: Which is one of the "deadly sins" in software security?
mcq.e: SQL injection is one of the deadly sins of software security. Neglecting change control is also a sin in the notes, so it is the closest confusion with the practices in the options.
x: Strong passwords are a recommended security practice, not one of the deadly sins of software security.
Code review is a recommended security practice, not a deadly sin of software security.
Change control is a management process, and the notes list neglecting it as a sin, so it is a close call, though SQL injection is the answer given.

mcq.q: Antiquated or outdated technologies leading to unreliable systems are a threat called:
mcq.e: Technological obsolescence is a threat from antiquated technology; good managerial planning should prevent it.
x: Technical hardware failure is a sudden equipment breakdown, not a threat from antiquated or outdated technology.
Theft is the unlawful taking of assets, not a threat from outdated technology.
Sabotage is deliberate damage or disruption, not a threat from antiquated technology.

mcq.q: Which statement about policy versus law is correct?
mcq.a: Ignorance of a policy is an acceptable defense
w: Ignorance of a policy is never an acceptable defense
Policies carry the authority of the state
Laws can be ignored if unknown
mcq.e: Per the notes, ignorance of a policy is an acceptable defense, unlike ignorance of the law. The reversed statement that it is never acceptable is the closest trap.
x: Ignorance of a policy is not always unacceptable; the notes say it is an acceptable defense, unlike ignorance of the law.
Policies are organizational rules and do not carry the authority of the state, which belongs to laws.
Laws cannot be ignored on the ground that they are unknown, so this statement is false.

mcq.q: Fixed moral attitudes or customs of a particular group are called:
mcq.e: Cultural mores are the fixed moral attitudes or customs of a particular group.
x: Laws are rules enforced by government, not informal moral attitudes or customs of a group.
Policies are organizational rules, not the fixed moral attitudes or customs of a particular group.
Codes are formal conduct or ethics guidelines, not the fixed moral attitudes or customs of a group.

mcq.q: The legal standard requiring a prudent organization to act legally and ethically and know the consequences of its actions is:
mcq.e: Due care means acting legally and ethically and knowing the consequences of one's actions. Due diligence is the closest confusion, since it adds maintaining that standard and making sure actions are effective.
x: Due diligence adds maintaining due care and making sure actions are effective, so it does not match the standard described.
Liability is legal responsibility for harm caused, not the standard of acting legally and ethically.
Jurisdiction is a court's authority to hear a case, not a standard of organizational conduct.

mcq.q: The legal standard requiring an organization to maintain due care and ensure its actions are effective is:
mcq.e: Due diligence means maintaining due care and making sure actions are effective. Due care is the closest confusion, since it only requires acting legally and ethically and knowing the consequences.
x: Due care only requires acting legally and ethically and knowing the consequences, without the requirement to ensure actions are effective.
Restitution is compensation to an injured party, not a standard of conduct for an organization.
Long-arm jurisdiction is the extension of a court's laws to outsiders, not a standard of conduct.

mcq.q: Compensating an injured party for wrongs committed is called:
mcq.e: Restitution is compensating an injured party for wrongs committed.
x: Jurisdiction is a court's authority over a case, not compensation to an injured party.
Mitigation is reducing the severity of risk or harm, not compensating an injured party.
Deterrence discourages illegal behavior through fear of penalties, not compensating an injured party.

mcq.q: Application of laws to those residing outside a court's normal jurisdiction is:
mcq.e: Long-arm jurisdiction applies a court's laws to those outside its normal reach.
x: Due care is a standard of acting legally and ethically, not the extension of a court's reach to outsiders.
Restitution is compensation for wrongs committed, not the application of laws to those outside a court's reach.
Liability is legal responsibility for harm, not the application of a court's laws to outsiders.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the five criteria for policy enforcement?
mcq.e: The five criteria are dissemination, review, comprehension, compliance and uniform enforcement, so retaliation is the one NOT on the list. Dissemination and uniform enforcement are on the list and are the closest distractors.
x: Dissemination is one of the five policy enforcement criteria, so it is on the list and is not the exception.
Comprehension is one of the five policy enforcement criteria, so it is on the list and is not the exception.
Uniform enforcement is one of the five policy enforcement criteria, so it is on the list and is not the exception.

mcq.q: Which U.S. law is the cornerstone of many computer-related federal laws?
mcq.a: Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986
mcq.e: The Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986 is the cornerstone of computer-crime law. The closest confusion is the 1996 NII Protection Act, which modified it, not the cornerstone itself.
x: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 governs financial reporting by public companies, not computer crime.
HIPAA of 1996 governs health information privacy, not the cornerstone of computer-related federal law.
The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act of 1999 governs financial privacy and services, not the cornerstone of computer crime law.

mcq.q: Which U.S. law is also known as the Kennedy-Kassebaum Act?
mcq.e: HIPAA (1996) is also known as the Kennedy-Kassebaum Act.
x: The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act is the Financial Services Modernization Act, covering financial institutions rather than health information.
The Freedom of Information Act gives public access to federal agency records, not health information privacy.
The Computer Security Act of 1987 set federal computer security standards and is not the Kennedy-Kassebaum Act.

mcq.q: Which law is the Financial Services Modernization Act?
mcq.e: The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (1999) is the Financial Services Modernization Act.
x: HIPAA is the Kennedy-Kassebaum Act on health information privacy, not the financial services modernization law.
The Sarbanes-Oxley Act governs reliable financial reporting by public companies, not financial services modernization.
The Federal Privacy Act governs personal records held by federal agencies, not financial services modernization.

mcq.q: Which law improves the reliability and accuracy of financial reporting of public companies?
mcq.e: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 aims at reliable financial reporting by public companies.
x: HIPAA governs health information privacy, not the reliability of public company financial reporting.
The Computer Security Act of 1987 set security standards for federal computer systems, not financial reporting reliability.
The Economic Espionage Act criminalizes economic espionage and trade secret theft, not financial reporting reliability.

mcq.q: The Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) was passed in:
mcq.e: The Freedom of Information Act was passed in 1966. The closest confusion is 1986, the year of the CFA Act and the Electronic Communications Privacy Act in the notes.
x: 1986 is the year of the US Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, not the year FOIA was passed.
1996 is not the year FOIA was originally passed, so it does not match the question.
2002 is the year of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, not the year FOIA was passed.

mcq.q: FOIA does NOT apply to:
mcq.a: State and local governments and private businesses
mcq.e: FOIA covers access to federal agency records only, not state, local or private entities, so those are what it does NOT apply to. Federal agencies is the closest distractor because FOIA does apply to them.
x: Federal agencies are exactly where FOIA applies, so they are not the exception the question asks for.
Federal records are the materials FOIA gives access to, so FOIA does apply to them.
Requests made in writing are the normal way to make a FOIA request, so this does not describe an exception.

mcq.q: Which U.S. agency oversees identity theft efforts and recommends placing a fraud alert?
mcq.e: The FTC coordinates identity-theft efforts, starting with an initial fraud alert.
x: The FBI investigates federal crimes, but it does not coordinate identity-theft efforts and recommend fraud alerts.
The Secret Service protects officials and investigates financial crimes, not identity-theft recovery coordination.
The NSA handles foreign signals intelligence and information assurance, not consumer identity-theft efforts.

mcq.q: Which law prohibits circumventing copyright protection and was a response to EU Directive 95/46/EC?
mcq.e: The DMCA prohibits circumventing copyright protections, and the slides give EU Directive 95/46/EC as its response, a point the notes flag to verify. The closest confusion is TRIPS, an international IP agreement.
x: TRIPS is an international intellectual property agreement, not a US law prohibiting circumvention of copyright protection.
The PATRIOT Act is an anti-terrorism law expanding surveillance powers, not a copyright circumvention law.
The Computer Fraud and Abuse Act is a computer crime law, not the copyright circumvention prohibition.

mcq.q: The UK's Computer Misuse Act was enacted in:
mcq.e: The UK Computer Misuse Act was enacted in 1990. The closest confusion is 1986, the year of the US CFA Act.
x: 1986 is the year of the US Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, not the UK Computer Misuse Act.
2003 is not the year the UK Computer Misuse Act was enacted, which was 1990.
2006 is not the year the UK Computer Misuse Act was enacted, which was 1990.

mcq.q: How many "computer misuse offenses" did the UK Computer Misuse Act 1990 define?
mcq.e: The UK Computer Misuse Act 1990 defines three offenses: unauthorized access, unauthorized access with intent to commit further offenses, and unauthorized acts that impair operation. The closest numeric confusion is the count of 2 or 4.
x: Does not match the three offenses defined by the UK Computer Misuse Act 1990.
Does not match the three offenses defined by the UK Computer Misuse Act 1990.
Does not match the three offenses defined by the UK Computer Misuse Act 1990.

mcq.q: Which international convention lacks realistic provisions for enforcement?
mcq.a: Council of Europe Convention on Cybercrime
mcq.e: The Council of Europe Convention on Cybercrime lacks realistic enforcement provisions.
x: WTO TRIPS is a trade-based intellectual property agreement, not a cybercrime convention.
The Geneva Conventions set humanitarian law for armed conflict, not cybercrime enforcement.
The Hague Conventions cover armed conflict and international legal matters, not cybercrime, so they do not fit.

mcq.q: Which agreement was the first significant international effort to protect intellectual property rights?
mcq.e: The slides call the WTO TRIPS agreement the first significant international effort to protect IP, a point the notes flag to verify. The Council of Europe Convention on Cybercrime is the closest international distractor, and it lacks enforcement provisions.
x: The DMCA is a US law, not the first significant international effort to protect intellectual property rights.
The Convention on Cybercrime is a Council of Europe treaty on cybercrime, not an intellectual property agreement.
The Wassenaar Arrangement controls exports of dual-use technologies, not intellectual property rights.

mcq.q: The Ten Commandments of Computer Ethics were produced by the:
mcq.e: The Ten Commandments of Computer Ethics come from the Computer Ethics Institute.
x: ACM is a computing society with its own code of ethics, not the producer of the Ten Commandments of Computer Ethics.
ISC2 is a certifying body for security professionals, not the producer of the Ten Commandments of Computer Ethics.
The SANS Institute is a security training organization, not the producer of the Ten Commandments of Computer Ethics.

mcq.q: The deterrence of illegal behavior requires all EXCEPT:
mcq.e: Deterrence needs fear of penalty, probability of being apprehended and probability that the penalty is applied. Low cost of enforcement is not one of these, so it is the EXCEPT answer.
x: Fear of penalty is an element of deterrence, so it is not the exception the question asks for.
Probability of being caught is an element of deterrence, so it is included and is not the exception.
Probability of the penalty being applied is an element of deterrence, so it is included and is not the exception.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the three general causes of unethical and illegal behavior?
mcq.e: The three causes are ignorance, accident and intent; poverty is not one.
x: Ignorance is one of the three general causes of unethical and illegal behavior, so it is not the exception.
Accident is one of the three general causes of unethical and illegal behavior, so it is not the exception.
Intent is one of the three general causes of unethical and illegal behavior, so it is not the exception.

mcq.q: The ACM was established in:
mcq.e: The ACM, the first educational and scientific computing society, was established in 1947. The closest confusion is 1993, which the notes give as the DEFCON year, not the ACM's.
x: Not the answer here: 1969 does not match the founding year of the ACM, which the notes place in 1947.
Not the answer here: 1985 does not match the founding year of the ACM, which the notes place in 1947.
1993 is the year the notes give for DEF CON, not the founding year of the ACM.

mcq.q: Which organization offers the GIAC certifications?
mcq.e: SANS offers the GIAC certifications.
x: ISACA offers the CISA and CISM certifications, not the GIAC certifications.
ISSA is a professional association for security practitioners, not the provider of GIAC certifications.
ACM is a computing society, not the provider of GIAC certifications.

mcq.q: Which organization offers CISSP and SSCP certifications?
mcq.e: (ISC)² offers the CISSP and SSCP certifications.
x: ISACA offers the CISA and CISM certifications, not the CISSP and SSCP certifications.
SANS offers the GIAC certifications, not the CISSP and SSCP certifications.
ACM is a computing society, not the certifying body for CISSP and SSCP.

mcq.q: The FBI program that maintains an intrusion alert network and secure website is:
mcq.e: The FBI's InfraGard program maintains an intrusion alert network and a secure website.
x: US-CERT is a DHS team for reporting incidents, not an FBI program maintaining an intrusion alert network.
TEMPEST covers standards for limiting electromagnetic emanations, not an intrusion alert network and secure website.
NIACAP is a DoD certification and accreditation process, not an FBI intrusion alert program.

mcq.q: Which U.S. agency's Information Assurance Directorate protects systems of high national value?
mcq.e: The NSA's Information Assurance Directorate protects systems of high national value.
x: The FBI is federal law enforcement, not the agency whose Information Assurance Directorate protects systems of high national value.
The Secret Service protects officials and investigates financial crimes, not national-value systems protection.
DHS is the Department of Homeland Security, which runs US-CERT, not the Information Assurance Directorate.

mcq.q: Which U.S. agency's team (US-CERT) provides mechanisms for reporting phishing and malware?
mcq.e: DHS's US-CERT provides mechanisms to report phishing and malware.
x: The FBI investigates crimes, but it does not run the US-CERT reporting team.
The NSA runs the Information Assurance Directorate, not the US-CERT reporting team.
The FTC is a consumer protection agency, not the team that runs US-CERT.

mcq.q: How many outcomes does information security governance have?
mcq.e: Governance has five outcomes: strategic alignment, risk management, resource management, performance measurement and value delivery. The closest numeric distractors are 3, 4 and 7.
x: Does not match the five governance outcomes: strategic alignment, risk management, resource management, performance measurement and value delivery.
Does not match the five governance outcomes listed in the notes.
Does not match the five governance outcomes listed in the notes.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a governance outcome?
mcq.e: Of the five governance outcomes (strategic alignment, risk management, resource management, performance measurement, value delivery), cost cutting is not one. Risk management and value delivery are on the list and are the closest distractors.
x: Strategic alignment is one of the five governance outcomes, so it is not the item that does not belong.
Risk management is one of the five governance outcomes, so it is not the item that does not belong.
Value delivery is one of the five governance outcomes, so it is not the item that does not belong.

mcq.q: Which are the least expensive controls to execute but the most difficult to implement properly?
mcq.e: Policies are the least expensive controls to execute but the most difficult to implement properly.
x: Firewalls are technical controls that are more costly to run than policies, so they are not the least expensive controls.
Biometrics are technical controls that cost more to execute than policies, so they are not the least expensive controls.
Encryption tools are technical controls with execution costs above those of policies, so they do not match the question.

mcq.q: Which policy sets the strategic direction, scope and tone for all security efforts and is drafted by or with the CIO?
mcq.e: The EISP sets strategic direction, scope and tone, and is drafted by or with the CIO.
x: The ISSP covers specific areas of technology, not the overall strategic direction, scope and tone of security efforts.
The SysSP holds standards and procedures for configuring systems, not the strategic direction of all security efforts.
The SETA program is a security education, training and awareness program, not the strategic policy for security efforts.

mcq.q: Which policy addresses specific areas of technology and requires frequent updates?
mcq.e: The ISSP covers specific technology areas and needs frequent updates.
x: The EISP sets the overall strategic direction and does not change frequently for specific technologies.
The SysSP covers standards and procedures for configuring systems, not specific technology areas that need frequent updates.
BIA is business impact analysis, a risk process rather than a policy type covering specific technology areas.

mcq.q: Which policy often functions as standards or procedures used to configure or maintain systems?
mcq.e: The SysSP holds standards and procedures for configuring or maintaining systems.
x: The EISP is the enterprise-wide strategic policy, not the standards used to configure or maintain systems.
The ISSP addresses specific technology areas in policy form, not configuration standards and procedures for systems.
The SETA program is an education, training and awareness effort, not the procedures used to configure or maintain systems.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the three common approaches to creating ISSPs?
mcq.e: The three approaches to creating ISSPs are independent documents, a single comprehensive document and a modular document. Hierarchical document is the closest-sounding distractor and is not on the notes' list.
x: Independent documents is one of the three common approaches to creating ISSPs, so it is on the list and is not the exception.
A single comprehensive document is one of the three common approaches to creating ISSPs, so it is on the list and is not the exception.
A modular document is one of the three common approaches to creating ISSPs, so it is on the list and is not the exception.

mcq.q: ISO/IEC 27001 deals with:
mcq.e: ISO/IEC 27001 specifies requirements for an information security management system (ISMS). ISO/IEC 27005, which covers risk management, is the closest confusion.
x: Risk management is the subject of ISO/IEC 27005, not ISO/IEC 27001, which specifies the ISMS requirements.
Cloud services are covered by ISO/IEC 27017 for cloud security controls, not by the ISMS standard in ISO/IEC 27001.
Digital evidence is covered by ISO/IEC 27037, not by the ISMS requirements in ISO/IEC 27001.

mcq.q: ISO/IEC 27005 deals with:
mcq.e: ISO/IEC 27005 covers information security risk management. ISO/IEC 27001, the ISMS requirements standard, is the closest confusion among the 27000-series numbers.
x: Governance of information security is covered by a different standard, ISO/IEC 27014, not by ISO/IEC 27005.
Network security is covered by ISO/IEC 27033, not by the risk management standard ISO/IEC 27005.
Incident management is covered by ISO/IEC 27035, not by the risk management standard ISO/IEC 27005.

mcq.q: ISO/IEC 27035 deals with:
mcq.e: ISO/IEC 27035 covers information security incident management. ISO/IEC 27037, which covers digital evidence, is the closest confusion because it is the adjacent number in the series.
x: Cybersecurity guidelines are covered by ISO/IEC 27032, not by the incident management standard ISO/IEC 27035.
Digital evidence collection is covered by ISO/IEC 27037, the adjacent standard, not by ISO/IEC 27035.
Health informatics is a separate ISO series, ISO 27799, and does not cover incident management.

mcq.q: ISO/IEC 27037 covers:
mcq.a: Collection and preservation of digital evidence
mcq.e: ISO/IEC 27037 covers identification, collection and preservation of digital evidence. ISO/IEC 27035, which covers incident management, is the closest confusion because it is the adjacent number in the series.
x: Cloud security is covered by ISO/IEC 27017 and 27018, not by the digital evidence standard ISO/IEC 27037.
Governance is covered by ISO/IEC 27014, not by the digital evidence standard ISO/IEC 27037.
Telecommunications security is covered by ISO/IEC 27011, not by the digital evidence standard ISO/IEC 27037.

mcq.q: Which NIST special publication sets out 33 principles for securing systems?
mcq.e: NIST SP 800-14 lists 33 principles for securing systems. SP 800-12 is the closest confusion; the notes list it among the NIST models without the 33 principles.
x: SP 800-12 is an introductory computer security handbook, not the publication listing 33 principles for securing systems.
SP 800-30 is the guide for conducting risk assessments, not the publication listing 33 principles.
SP 800-64 covers security considerations in the system development life cycle, not the 33 principles.

mcq.q: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework consists of:
mcq.e: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework has three components: framework core, tiers and profile.
x: Identify, protect and detect are three of the five core functions inside the framework core, not the three top-level components the question asks for.
Plan, do, check is the generic Plan-Do-Check-Act improvement cycle, not a component of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
People, process and technology is a general way to group security concerns, not the NIST framework components, which are core, tiers and profile.

mcq.q: Which level of controls addresses personnel and physical security?
mcq.e: Operational controls address personnel and physical security.
x: Management controls are administrative controls such as policy, planning and risk management, not personnel and physical security controls.
Technical controls are logical controls built into systems, such as access control, encryption and firewalls, not personnel or physical security.
Legal controls are not one of the three control levels (management, operational and technical), so they do not fit this classification.

mcq.q: A security perimeter does NOT protect against:
mcq.e: A security perimeter protects from outside attack but not from attacks by insiders.
x: External hackers are exactly what a security perimeter is designed to block, so the perimeter does protect against them.
Port scans from outside are detected or filtered at the perimeter by firewalls and monitoring, so the perimeter does guard against them.
Spoofed packets are commonly dropped at the perimeter by filtering routers and firewalls, so the perimeter does protect against them.

mcq.q: SETA stands for:
mcq.e: SETA is Security Education, Training and Awareness.
x: Systems Engineering and Technical Assessment is not what SETA stands for; SETA is Security Education, Training and Awareness.
Security Evaluation and Threat Analysis is not what SETA stands for; it names a risk activity, not the security education program.
Secure Enterprise Technology Architecture is not what SETA stands for; it describes an architecture, not the security education program.

mcq.q: In SETA, which element answers "why" and has a long-term impact?
mcq.e: Education answers "why", is theoretical, and has the longest-term impact.
x: Training teaches specific skills and how to perform tasks, so it answers how rather than why and has a shorter-term impact.
Awareness raises attention to security issues through media, so it is short term and does not explain why.
Compliance is not one of the three SETA elements; it is a regulatory obligation, so it is not the answer here.

mcq.q: In SETA, which element is delivered through videos, newsletters and posters?
mcq.e: Awareness uses media such as videos, newsletters and posters and has short-term impact.
x: Training teaches specific skills through hands-on instruction, not through videos, newsletters and posters.
Education is theoretical and long term, delivered through in-depth learning rather than posters or newsletters.
Certification is a formal credential, not one of the three SETA elements, so it does not match this question.

mcq.q: Which plan focuses on the immediate response to an attack?
mcq.e: The incident response plan covers the immediate response to an attack.
x: Disaster recovery plan restores systems and operations at the primary site after a major disaster, not the immediate response to an attack.
Business continuity plan keeps critical business functions running and relocates operations, not the immediate response to an attack.
Security policy is a high-level statement of rules and management intent, not an operational plan for responding to an attack.

mcq.q: Which plan reestablishes operations at the primary site after a disaster?
mcq.e: The disaster recovery plan restores operations at the primary site after a disaster.
x: Business continuity plan keeps or relocates critical business functions, but it does not focus on reestablishing operations at the primary site.
Incident response plan handles the immediate response to an attack, not the recovery of operations at the primary site after a disaster.
Acquisition plan covers procurement of resources, not disaster recovery, so it does not fit a question about restoring the primary site.

mcq.q: Which plan prepares the organization to reestablish or relocate critical business operations?
mcq.e: The business continuity plan reestablishes or relocates critical operations during a disaster. The disaster recovery plan is the closest confusion, since it restores systems and reestablishes operations at the primary site.
x: Disaster recovery plan restores systems and reestablishes operations at the primary site, the closest confusion, but it does not relocate critical operations as this question asks.
Incident response plan handles the immediate response to an attack, not the reestablishment or relocation of critical business operations.
Risk management plan identifies and manages risks in general, not the reestablishment or relocation of critical operations after a disaster.

mcq.q: What is the first step in the contingency planning process?
mcq.e: The first step of the CP process is developing the CP policy statement, and conducting the BIA comes second. Conduct the BIA is the closest distractor because it is the second step.
x: Conduct the BIA is the second step, after developing the CP policy statement, so it is not the first step.
Identify preventive controls comes after the business impact analysis in the CP process, so it is not the first step.
Create contingency strategies is a later step, after the BIA and controls are identified, so it is not the first step.

mcq.q: The investigation and assessment of adverse events assuming controls have failed is the:
mcq.e: The BIA investigates the impact of adverse events as if controls had failed, to prioritize recovery.
x: Risk assessment identifies and evaluates risks with current controls in place, not the impact of events assuming controls have failed.
Threat assessment identifies sources of threats and their likelihood, not the impact analysis of adverse events with failed controls.
Vulnerability scan is an automated check for weaknesses in systems, not an analysis of the impact of adverse events.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a BIA stage?
w: Determine mission/business processes and recovery criticality
Identify recovery priorities for system resources
mcq.e: The three BIA stages are determining mission/business processes and recovery criticality, identifying recovery priorities for system resources, and identifying resource requirements. Testing the disaster plan belongs to a separate contingency step, so it is the NOT answer.
x: Determine mission/business processes and recovery criticality is one of the three BIA stages, so it is not the excluded stage.
Identify recovery priorities for system resources is one of the three BIA stages, so it is not the excluded stage.
Identify resource requirements is one of the three BIA stages, so it is not the excluded stage.

mcq.q: Which is the FIRST priority in incident reaction?
mcq.e: Containment is the first priority in incident reaction.
x: Prosecution is legal action that follows the incident and is not the first priority during incident reaction.
Public announcement is a communication step handled after containment, so it is not the first priority.
Software upgrade is a recovery or eradication action that comes after containment, so it is not the first priority.

mcq.q: Which is NOT an exclusive-use site option in business continuity?
mcq.e: Time-share is a shared option; exclusive-use sites are hot, warm and cold.
x: Hot site is an exclusive-use site fully equipped and ready to run quickly, so it is an exclusive option rather than a shared one.
Warm site is an exclusive-use facility with partial equipment, so it is an exclusive option and not the one the question excludes.
Cold site is an exclusive-use facility with power and space but no equipment, so it is an exclusive option and does not fit the NOT question.

mcq.q: Which is a shared-use continuity option?
mcq.e: Mutual agreements are a shared option; hot, warm and cold sites are exclusive.
x: Hot site is an exclusive-use facility dedicated to one organization, so it is not a shared-use option.
Warm site is an exclusive-use facility with partial equipment, so it is not a shared-use option.
Cold site is an empty exclusive-use facility that needs equipment installed, so it is not a shared-use option.

mcq.q: Electronic vaulting, remote journaling and database shadowing are options for:
mcq.e: Electronic vaulting, remote journaling and database shadowing are off-site data storage options.
x: Intrusion detection monitors systems for attacks, not off-site storage of copies of data.
Network access control decides who and what can connect to a network, not how data copies are stored off site.
Data classification labels information by sensitivity, not a method of storing backups off site.

mcq.q: Which is a disadvantage of involving law enforcement?
mcq.a: The organization loses control of the chain of events
mcq.e: A disadvantage of law enforcement is that the organization loses control of the chain of events. The other options (better evidence handling, warrants, witness statements) are advantages, which is the trap.
x: This is an advantage of involving law enforcement, since they handle evidence with trained procedures, not a disadvantage.
Warrants being handled is an advantage of involving law enforcement, since they manage legal process, not a disadvantage.
Witness statements being obtained is an advantage of involving law enforcement, not a disadvantage.

mcq.q: Knowing yourself and knowing the enemy refers to understanding:
mcq.e: "Know yourself" means know your assets; "know the enemy" means know your threats.
x: Policies and procedures are governance documents, not the assets and threats that the know yourself and know the enemy phrase refers to.
Hackers and insiders only narrows threats to two sources, but the principle covers all assets and all types of threats.
Budget and schedule are project management concerns, not the assets and threats the phrase refers to.

mcq.q: The quantity and nature of risk that an organization is willing to accept is the:
mcq.e: Risk appetite is the quantity and nature of risk the organization will accept. Residual risk is the closest confusion; it is the risk remaining after controls are applied, not the amount accepted.
x: Residual risk is the risk remaining after controls, not the amount of risk the organization is willing to accept.
Risk transfer shifts risk to a third party such as an insurer, not the amount of risk the organization accepts.
Risk exposure is the potential loss or harm from a risk, not the quantity and nature of risk the organization accepts.

mcq.q: The risk remaining after current controls have been applied is:
mcq.e: Residual risk is the risk remaining after current controls are applied, and the goal is to bring it in line with risk appetite. Risk appetite is the closest confusion, since it is the amount of risk accepted rather than what remains.
x: Inherent risk is the risk before any controls are applied, not the risk remaining after current controls.
Total risk is not the standard term for the risk remaining after current controls; that is residual risk.
Accepted risk is the risk management decides to live with after evaluation, not the risk remaining after controls are applied.

mcq.q: Which three-level data classification scheme is used in the slides?
mcq.e: The slides classify data as confidential, internal or public.
x: Red, yellow and green is a traffic-light style scheme, not the three-level data classification used in the slides.
Low, medium and high is an impact rating scale, not the confidential, internal and public classification in the slides.
Open, closed and hybrid describe access or system models, not the three-level data classification in the slides.

mcq.q: A policy that requires removing sensitive documents from desks is a:
mcq.e: A clean desk policy requires sensitive documents to be put away when not in use.
x: Open door policy is a management practice of making managers accessible to employees, not a rule about where sensitive documents are kept.
Zero trust policy assumes no implicit trust and verifies each access request, not how sensitive documents are handled on desks.
Retention policy sets how long records are kept, not whether sensitive documents are left out on desks.

mcq.q: Searching through trash for sensitive information is:
mcq.e: Dumpster diving is searching trash for sensitive information.
x: Shoulder surfing is watching someone enter or read sensitive information over their shoulder, not searching through trash.
Tailgating is following an authorized person through a secured door without credentials, not searching through trash.
Baiting is leaving a lure, such as an infected device, to trick someone, not searching through trash.

mcq.q: Ranking assets using criteria weights that total 100 is:
mcq.e: Weighted factor analysis scores assets against criteria whose weights total 100.
x: Cost-benefit analysis compares the cost of a safeguard with the loss it prevents, not a weighted score of assets against criteria.
Baselining compares current security settings against a standard over time, not a weighted ranking of assets.
Benchmarking compares practices with other organizations or standards, not a weighted ranking of assets.

mcq.q: A TVA worksheet combines:
mcq.e: A TVA worksheet pairs threats, vulnerabilities and assets.
x: Technology, value and access does not match the TVA worksheet, which pairs threats, vulnerabilities and assets.
Time, volume and availability does not match the TVA worksheet, which pairs threats, vulnerabilities and assets.
Training, verification and audit does not match the TVA worksheet, which pairs threats, vulnerabilities and assets.

mcq.q: In relative risk assessment, risk equals:
mcq.a: Loss frequency times loss magnitude, minus mitigation, plus uncertainty
mcq.e: Relative risk is loss frequency times loss magnitude, minus the percentage mitigated by current controls, plus uncertainty. Threat plus vulnerability is the closest distractor, but it is a different pairing from the notes.
x: Threat plus vulnerability is a simplified pairing, not the relative risk formula given in the notes, which uses frequency, magnitude, mitigation and uncertainty.
Asset value divided by exposure is not the relative risk formula; asset value times exposure factor gives single loss expectancy.
Loss magnitude only ignores loss frequency, mitigation and uncertainty, so it is not the relative risk formula.

mcq.q: Which risk control strategy is the preferred approach and attempts to prevent exploitation of vulnerabilities?
mcq.e: Defense, the preferred strategy, uses policy, education and technology to prevent exploitation.
x: Transference shifts risk to another party such as an insurer, so it does not prevent exploitation of the vulnerability.
Acceptance leaves the vulnerability unaddressed and accepts the outcome, so it does not prevent exploitation.
Termination ends the risky business activity entirely, which is used when risk cannot be controlled, not the preferred prevention approach.

mcq.q: Shifting risk to another organization, such as outsourcing or insurance, is:
mcq.e: Transference shifts risk to another organization, for example through outsourcing or insurance.
x: Mitigation reduces the impact of an attack through plans and controls while the organization keeps the risk, so it does not shift risk.
Acceptance takes no action on the risk, so it does not shift risk to another organization.
Termination ends the risky activity rather than shifting the risk to another organization.

mcq.q: Reducing the impact of an attack (IR, DR, BC plans) rather than preventing it is:
mcq.e: Mitigation reduces the impact of an attack through IR, DR and BC plans.
x: Defense aims to prevent exploitation of vulnerabilities, not to reduce the impact of an attack after it happens.
Acceptance takes no action on the risk, so it does not reduce impact through plans.
Transference shifts risk to another organization, not a way to reduce its impact through IR, DR and BC plans.

mcq.q: Doing nothing to protect a vulnerability and accepting the outcome is:
mcq.e: Acceptance means doing nothing about the vulnerability and accepting the outcome, valid only when the asset does not justify the cost of protection.
x: Termination avoids the business activity that creates the risk, so it is not doing nothing about the vulnerability.
Mitigation takes active steps such as IR, DR and BC plans to reduce impact, not doing nothing.
Defense takes active prevention steps through policy, education and technology, not doing nothing about the vulnerability.

mcq.q: Avoiding business activities that introduce uncontrollable risks is:
mcq.e: Termination avoids the business activity that introduces uncontrollable risk.
x: Acceptance means doing nothing about the risk and living with the outcome, not avoiding the risky activity.
Transference shifts the risk to another party rather than avoiding the business activity that creates it.
Defense prevents exploitation of vulnerabilities while keeping the activity, not avoiding the activity altogether.

mcq.q: What is the most common mitigation procedure?
mcq.e: The disaster recovery plan is the most common mitigation procedure. Incident response and business continuity are the closest distractors, since they are the other mitigation plans.
x: Incident response plan is also a mitigation plan, but it handles immediate attack response, and the notes name the disaster recovery plan as the most common.
Business continuity plan is another mitigation plan, but it is not the most common procedure named in the notes.
Security policy is a governance document of rules, not a mitigation procedure for reducing the impact of an attack.

mcq.q: SLE is computed as:
mcq.e: Single loss expectancy is asset value times exposure factor (SLE = AV × EF).
x: ALE times ARO is the annualized loss formula, which uses SLE as an input, so it does not compute SLE itself.
Asset value divided by ARO does not compute single loss expectancy; SLE is asset value times exposure factor.
Threat times vulnerability is a qualitative pairing, not the formula for single loss expectancy.

mcq.q: ALE is computed as:
mcq.e: Annualized loss expectancy is SLE times the annualized rate of occurrence (ALE = SLE × ARO).
x: Asset value times exposure factor gives single loss expectancy, which is per event, not the annualized loss.
SLE divided by ARO divides instead of multiplying by the annual rate, so it does not give ALE.
ACS times exposure factor does not match the ALE formula; ACS is the annual cost of a safeguard, not a loss input.

mcq.q: The cost-benefit analysis formula is:
mcq.e: Cost-benefit analysis is ALE(prior) minus ALE(post) minus ACS, the annualized loss reduction minus the annualized cost of the safeguard. The sign-flipped ALE(post) minus ALE(prior) plus ACS is the closest confusion.
x: ALE(post) minus ALE(prior) plus ACS is the sign-flipped version, which measures the wrong direction of loss reduction.
SLE times ARO minus ACS uses only the loss before the safeguard, so it does not measure the reduction after the safeguard.
Asset value minus EF does not compute cost-benefit; EF is a fraction and is not subtracted from asset value.

mcq.q: ARO stands for:
mcq.e: ARO is the annualized rate of occurrence, how often the loss event is expected per year.
x: Annual risk objective is not the standard meaning of ARO in loss expectancy calculations.
Asset recovery option is not the meaning of ARO here; ARO is the annualized rate of occurrence.
Average rate of overload is not the ARO term; ARO is the annualized rate of occurrence of a loss event.

mcq.q: Assessment using nonnumerical scales rather than actual values is:
mcq.e: Qualitative assessment uses scales rather than actual numeric values; quantitative assessment uses actual values.
x: Quantitative assessment uses actual numeric values rather than nonnumerical scales, so it is the opposite approach.
Baselining compares current security against past or standard performance, not a scale-based assessment method.
Benchmarking compares practices with other organizations, not a method that uses nonnumerical scales.

mcq.q: The biggest problem with benchmarking is that:
mcq.a: Organizations don't talk to each other
mcq.e: The slides say the biggest problem with benchmarking is that organizations do not talk to each other.
x: It is too cheap is not the stated biggest problem with benchmarking in the slides.
It uses numbers only is not the stated problem; benchmarking does not depend on numbers alone.
It ignores security is not the stated problem; benchmarking is itself a security comparison method.

mcq.q: Comparison of past security activities against future performance is:
mcq.e: Baselining compares past security activities and performance with future performance.
x: Benchmarking compares security against other organizations or standards, not against the organization's own past performance.
Termination avoids a risky business activity, not a comparison of past and future security performance.
Mitigation reduces the impact of an attack, not a comparison of past and future security performance.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a feasibility study type in the slides?
mcq.e: The slide feasibility studies are organizational, operational, technical and political, plus economic via CBA. Legal is the one NOT listed, and organizational and political are the closest listed types.
x: Organizational feasibility is one of the feasibility study types listed in the slides, so it is not the excluded one.
Operational feasibility is one of the feasibility study types listed in the slides, so it is not the excluded one.
Political feasibility is one of the feasibility study types listed in the slides, so it is not the excluded one.

mcq.q: The four steps of the NIST risk management process (SP 800-39) are:
mcq.e: The NIST SP 800-39 risk management process is frame, assess, respond, monitor. The SP 800-37 RMF steps (categorize, select, implement, assess, authorize, monitor) are the closest confusion, and the notes warn against mixing them.
x: Plan, do, check, act is the PDCA improvement cycle, not the NIST SP 800-39 risk management process.
Identify, protect, detect, respond are NIST CSF core functions, not the four SP 800-39 steps.
Prepare, categorize, select, implement are early steps of the SP 800-37 RMF, not the four SP 800-39 steps.

mcq.q: Which type of access control is implemented at the discretion of the data user?
mcq.e: DAC is implemented at the discretion of the data user.
x: MAC is system-enforced access based on classification labels, not access decided at the discretion of the data user.
Nondiscretionary access is set by central rules rather than the data user's discretion, so it is not the answer.
RBAC grants access based on job roles assigned by the organization, not at the data user's discretion.

mcq.q: Which access control uses a structured data classification scheme rating both information and users?
mcq.e: MAC uses a structured data classification scheme that rates both collections of information and users.
x: DAC lets data owners decide access without a classification scheme, so it does not rate both information and users.
Nondiscretionary control is a broader category set by central rules, not the structured classification scheme rating information and users.
ACL is a list of permissions attached to a resource, not a structured classification scheme rating information and users.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the four fundamental functions of access control?
mcq.e: The four functions are identification, authentication, authorization and accountability; encryption is not one.
x: Identification is one of the four fundamental functions, where a user claims an identity, so it is not the excluded one.
Authorization is one of the four fundamental functions, which grants permitted actions, so it is not the excluded one.
Accountability is one of the four fundamental functions, which tracks user actions, so it is not the excluded one.

mcq.q: "I am a user of the system" describes:
mcq.e: Identification is the claim "I am a user of the system".
x: Authentication is proving the claimed identity, not making the claim itself.
Authorization decides what an authenticated user may do, not the act of claiming identity.
Accountability tracks and records user actions, not the act of claiming identity.

mcq.q: "I can prove I'm a user of the system" describes:
mcq.e: Authentication is proving you are who you claim to be.
x: Identification is the claim of who you are, not the proof that the claim is true.
Authorization decides what an authenticated user may access, not the proof of identity.
Accountability records and tracks actions through logs, not the proof of identity.

mcq.q: "You can track and monitor my use of the system" describes:
mcq.e: Accountability means use of the system can be tracked and audited through logs and journals.
x: Identification is stating who you are, not tracking use of the system.
Authentication verifies that a claimed identity is valid, not tracking use of the system.
Authorization decides what a user may access, not tracking and monitoring of use.

mcq.q: A password is an example of which authentication factor?
mcq.e: A password is something you know.
x: Something you have is a physical item such as a token or card, not a secret the user knows.
Something you are is a biometric trait such as a fingerprint, not a secret the user knows.
Somewhere you are is a location-based factor, not a secret the user knows.

mcq.q: A smart card is an example of:
mcq.e: A smart card (chip card) is something you have.
x: Something you know is a secret such as a password or PIN, not a physical item like a smart card.
Something you are is a biometric trait such as a fingerprint, not a physical item carried by the user.
Something you do is a behavioral trait such as typing rhythm, not a physical item like a smart card.

mcq.q: A series of characters longer than a password, from which a virtual password is derived, is a:
mcq.e: A passphrase is a longer string of characters from which a virtual password is derived.
x: PIN is a short numeric code, not a longer character string from which a virtual password is derived.
Token is a device or software that generates codes, not a character string from which a password is derived.
Salt is random data added before hashing, not a character string from which a virtual password is derived.

mcq.q: Which biometric characteristics are considered truly unique in the slides?
mcq.e: Only fingerprints, retina, iris and DNA are considered truly unique. Voice, signature and gait are the closest distractors, since they are biometric traits but not on the slides' unique list.
x: Voice, signature and gait are behavioral or variable traits, not on the slides' truly unique list.
Face and keystroke only is not the truly unique set; face is not on the unique list and keystroke dynamics is behavioral.
Hand geometry and odor are not on the slides' truly unique list, so they do not fit this question.

mcq.q: The point where false reject rate equals false accept rate is the:
mcq.e: The crossover error rate is where the false reject rate equals the false accept rate.
x: Failure rate is a general measure of failed attempts, not the point where the false reject rate and false accept rate are equal.
Match rate is not the standard term for this point; it does not describe where FRR equals FAR.
Equal acceptance rate is not the standard term; the point where FRR equals FAR is the crossover error rate.

mcq.q: The Bell-LaPadula model's principle is:
mcq.a: No read up, no write down
w: No write up, no read down
mcq.e: Bell-LaPadula is the confidentiality model: no read up, no write down. Biba's no write up, no read down is the reversed closest confusion, and it belongs to integrity.
x: No write up, no read down is the Biba integrity rule, the reverse of the Bell-LaPadula confidentiality rule.
Read only is a simple access mode, not the Bell-LaPadula principle about reading and writing across levels.
Need to know is a compartment access principle, not the Bell-LaPadula no read up, no write down rule.

mcq.q: The Biba model's principle is:
mcq.a: No write up, no read down
w: No read up, no write down
mcq.e: Biba is the integrity model: no write up, no read down. Bell-LaPadula's no read up, no write down is the reversed closest confusion, and it belongs to confidentiality.
x: No read up, no write down is the Bell-LaPadula confidentiality rule, not the Biba integrity rule.
Least privilege is a general principle of granting minimum access, not the Biba rule.
Separation of duties is a control principle that splits critical tasks, not the Biba rule.

mcq.q: Which model is a confidentiality model?
mcq.e: Bell-LaPadula is the confidentiality model; Biba and Clark-Wilson address integrity.
x: Biba is an integrity model, not a confidentiality model.
Clark-Wilson is an integrity model using well-formed transactions, not a confidentiality model.
Common Criteria is an evaluation standard for security products, not an access control model.

mcq.q: Which model is the successor to both TCSEC and ITSEC?
mcq.e: The Common Criteria succeeded TCSEC and ITSEC.
x: Clark-Wilson is an integrity model, not the successor to TCSEC and ITSEC.
Graham-Denning is an access control model, not the successor to TCSEC and ITSEC.
Bell-LaPadula is a confidentiality model, not the successor to TCSEC and ITSEC.

mcq.q: Covert channels in the trusted computing base include:
mcq.e: Covert channels in the trusted computing base are storage channels and timing channels.
x: Network and host channels are not the covert channel types the notes give for the trusted computing base.
Wired and wireless channels are media distinctions, not the covert channel types for the trusted computing base.
Public and private channels are not the covert channel types for the trusted computing base.

mcq.q: Which firewall type examines packet headers such as source/destination IP and ports?
mcq.e: Packet-filtering firewalls examine header fields such as source and destination IP address, direction and TCP/UDP port.
x: Application proxy works at the application layer and inspects content, not only packet headers.
Honeypot is a decoy system for luring attackers, not a firewall that examines packet headers.
Content filter restricts content categories rather than examining packet header fields.

mcq.q: Which packet-filtering firewall tracks connections using a state table?
